title: Desloratadine Induces TP53-Dependent Apoptosis in MCF-7 Breast Cancer Cells.
authors: Kabir, Syed Rashel; Abdullah, Taufique; Azam, Gausul; Molla, Tamzid Hossain; Ali, Hasan; Miah, Mojnu; Alam, Mohammad Taufiq; Miah, Sayem
one_liner_zh: 该文研究地氯雷他定在MCF-7乳腺癌细胞中诱导p53依赖性凋亡，虽含分子对接但对象为药物-蛋白结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of mortality among women despite advances in early detection and targeted therapies, underscoring the need for safer and more effective treatment options. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy by leveraging existing pharmacological agents with established safety profiles. Desloratadine, a second-generation H1-histamine receptor antagonist widely prescribed for allergic conditions, has attracted interest in oncology because histamine signaling influences proliferation, angiogenesis, and immune responses, yet its anticancer potential remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated its effects in MCF-7 breast cancer cells, which harbor wild-type TP53. Desloratadine inhibited cell viability in a dose-dependent manner, with an IC(50) of 14.2 microg/mL. Mechanistic analyses revealed that growth inhibition was primarily mediated through apoptosis, confirmed by Hoechst 33342 staining, ROS generation, annexin V/PI staining, and caspase-dependent pathways. Gene expression profiling demonstrated upregulation of TP53, FAS, and BAX, alongside reduced PARP-1 and NF-kappaB expression, with no detectable STAT3 or BCL2 expression. Flow cytometry indicated accumulation of cells in the sub-G(1) phase and G(2)/M arrest, consistent with apoptosis induction. Molecular docking further supported these findings, showing that Desloratadine binds with high affinity to p53 (-7.0 kcal/mol), FAS (-6.8 kcal/mol), and NF-kappaB (-6.5 kcal/mol), forming stabilizing hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions aligned with the observed gene expression changes. To confirm the functional role of TP53, we generated CRISPR-Cas9 knockout MCF-7 cells. Compared with wild-type cells, these knockout cells displayed markedly reduced sensitivity to Desloratadine, with the IC(50) shifting from 14.2 microg/mL to 36.4 microg/mL, demonstrating that p53 is a key mediator of the drug's cytotoxic effect. Collectively, these findings identify Desloratadine as a potential repurposed drug candidate for breast cancer therapy, acting at least in part through a p53-dependent apoptotic pathway.
abstract_zh: 尽管早期检测和靶向治疗取得了进展，乳腺癌仍然是女性死亡的主要原因，这凸显了对更安全、更有效治疗选择的需求。药物再利用通过利用具有既定安全性的现有药理制剂，提供了一种有前景的策略。地氯雷他定（Desloratadine）是一种第二代H1-组胺受体拮抗剂，广泛用于过敏性疾病，因其组胺信号影响增殖、血管生成和免疫反应，在肿瘤学领域引起了关注，但其抗癌潜力仍知之甚少。在本研究中，我们调查了其在含有野生型TP53的MCF-7乳腺癌细胞中的效应。地氯雷他定以剂量依赖性方式抑制细胞活力，其IC(50)为14.2微克/毫升。机制分析揭示，生长抑制主要通过凋亡介导，这通过Hoechst 33342染色、ROS生成、annexin V/PI染色和caspase依赖性通路得到确认。基因表达谱分析显示TP53、FAS和BAX表达上调，同时PARP-1和NF-kappaB表达降低，且未检测到STAT3或BCL2表达。流式细胞术显示细胞在sub-G(1)期积累和G(2)/M期阻滞，与凋亡诱导一致。分子对接进一步支持了这些发现，显示地氯雷他定以高亲和力结合p53（-7.0 kcal/mol）、FAS（-6.8 kcal/mol）和NF-kappaB（-6.5 kcal/mol），形成稳定的氢键和疏水相互作用，与观察到的基因表达变化一致。为确认TP53的功能作用，我们生成了CRISPR-Cas9敲除MCF-7细胞。与野生型细胞相比，这些敲除细胞对地氯雷他定的敏感性显著降低，IC(50)从14.2微克/毫升变为36.4微克/毫升，证明p53是该药物细胞毒性效应的关键介导因子。综合来看，这些发现将地氯雷他定确定为乳腺癌治疗的潜在再利用药物候选，其作用至少部分通过p53依赖性凋亡通路实现。
